rationale: Across multiple independent cohorts describing spinocerebellar ataxia 52 (SCA52; OMIM #621535), the recurrent heterozygous RAB3A hotspot mutation c.247C>T p.(Arg83Trp) consistently presents as adult-onset, gradually progressive cerebellar ataxia with cerebellar cortical and vermian atrophy. It is not an obligate early-infantile-onset ataxia with mandatory hypotonia. Early reports or suggestions of severe early neurodevelopmental phenotypes in RAB3A are primarily associated with distinct unique de novo or loss-of-function variants rather than the recurrent p.Arg83Trp missense variant.

evidence.text: Screening of ataxia cohorts identified 18 individuals from 10 unrelated families presenting with cerebellar ataxia, 9 of which carried the recurrent heterozygous RAB3A p.Arg83Trp variant associated with pure cerebellar ataxia, whereas separate neurodevelopmental phenotypes were linked to distinct de novo or loss-of-function variants.

source.title: Heterozygous RAB3A variants cause cerebellar ataxia by a partial loss-of-function mechanism
source.quote: In total, we identified 18 individuals from 10 unrelated families all sharing a cerebellar ataxia phenotype. Notably, 9 of the 10 families carried a recurrent variant in RAB3A, p.Arg83Trp, including one de novo occurrence.

evidence.text: Affected individuals from two independent families harboring the heterozygous c.247C>T p.(Arg83Trp) variant developed adult-onset, gradually progressive cerebellar symptoms accompanied by mild spasticity and tremor, with neuroimaging showing cerebellar atrophy accentuated in the vermis and neuropathology demonstrating cerebellar cortical degeneration.

source.title: An R83W mutation in Rab3A causes autosomal-dominant cerebellar ataxia
source.quote: Affected individuals presented with adult-onset, gradually progressive cerebellar symptoms, often accompanied by mild gait spasticity and tremors. Variable features of neurodevelopmental disorders were also observed. Brain MRI consistently revealed cerebellar atrophy, often accentuated in the vermis

evidence.text: Patients carrying the RAB3A p.Arg83Trp mutation developed slowly progressive gait ataxia beginning in their fourth decade of life (adult-onset).

source.title: RAB3A variants in ataxia and other neurodegenerative disorders
source.quote: Both patients developed slowly progressive gait ataxia beginning in their fourth decade of life

new_directions.question_text: What is the penetrance and spectrum of subclinical pyramidal signs (spasticity) versus pure cerebellar ataxia across different age brackets in RAB3A p.Arg83Trp carriers?
new_directions.rationale: Several reports note mild gait spasticity or an overlap with spastic paraplegia, indicating a phenotypic continuum within the ataxia-spasticity spectrum.
